methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $356M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Gatik, a Series C autonomous transportation company founded by Gautam and Arjun Narang, has raised $356M to date. The private frontier-tech transportation sector includes 8 identified peers spanning autonomous vehicles and related infrastructure; public comparables are absent, limiting traditional public-market triangulation.

Stage-progression methodology applies here given the Series C inflection point. Using total raised ($356M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of progression to the next funding stage yields $605M. This method is applicable given the availability of funding history and standard venture-stage progression norms, though it does not reflect operational metrics or market dynamics specific to autonomous transportation. Peer-median analysis does not apply: while 8 private peers exist in Transportation (including Rivian, Einride, and ZeroAvia), no subset of same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meets the three-datapoint threshold required for statistical reliability.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $514M to $695M, anchored to a median of $605M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the absence of operational benchmarks (unit economics, fleet deployment metrics), limited peer-group homogeneity within autonomous transportation, and the nascent nature of commercial deployment milestones in the sector. Revenue multiples and profitability remain unmeasured. Validation would benefit from access to internal metrics, customer traction, and a denser peer dataset at comparable funding stages.
